*** THE GRANADA MARRIAGE - THE BEST FIND OF THE PASS ***
column2: *** "LERENA y ARMENTA Sancho - Spouse: de AGUILAR Ana Maria - Marriage between 1725 and 1775 - GRANADA, SPAIN" *** - and it appears in TWO INDEPENDENT ARCHIVE COLLECTIONS, the "Index des mariages catholique de Grenade" and "Spain, Marriages, 1565-1950". These are indexed ARCHIVE records, not somebody's tree
column3: SECONDARY - two indexes read, no image opened
column4: *** THIS IS WHERE "AGUILAR" COMES FROM, and this archive spent all of today calling it unattested. *** Fourteen Uruguayan records name Sancho and NOT ONE gives him a matronymic; "Llerena y Aguilar" was marked as coming from a tree and from nowhere read here. *** A SON of Sancho Lerena y Armenta and Ana Maria de Aguilar would be styled LERENA y AGUILAR - which is exactly the name the trees give our Sancho, born 1767. *** The trees were following a real Spanish naming rule, not inventing a surname.

column1: *** AND IT MOVES THE SPANISH QUESTION FROM CORDOBA TO GRANADA ***
column2: The Uruguayan census of 1726-1858 says Sancho was born in *** "ANDALUZIA" ***. The Geneanet TREES say *** CORDOBA *** - one, ckurti, says *** ZUHEROS, CORDOBA *** specifically. This marriage says *** GRANADA ***
column3: Census PRIMARY; trees SECONDARY; marriage index SECONDARY
column4: *** Granada and Cordoba are both in ANDALUSIA, so nothing contradicts the census. *** But the archive's open question - "Basque or Extremaduran?" - now has a THIRD answer on the table and a testable one: a named parish index in the Diocese of Granada. *** And the surname's own home town of LLERENA is in EXTREMADURA, which is NOT Andalusia - a tension this archive has recorded and still cannot resolve. ***

column1: *** A DEATH DATE FOR SANCHO ***
column2: *** 1832 *** - given by four separate trees (jfina, abal2018, ckurti, fpaillusseau)
column4: *** THIS ARCHIVE HAS NO DEATH DATE FOR HIM AT ALL. *** His last dated record here is his son's marriage petition of 3 September 1836 - which, if 1832 is right, is FOUR YEARS AFTER HE DIED and would make that act's "hijo legitimo de D. Sancho Lerena" a reference to a dead man, which is ordinary. *** Worth testing against Montevideo burials, and NOT adopted. ***

column1: *** HIS WIFE'S FULLER NAME ***
column2: The trees give *** MARIA JOSEFA (TERESA) FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS ***
column4: The 1830 marriage act read here today says only "MARIA FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS". The trees add JOSEFA and, in two of them, TERESA. *** The act already vindicated the trees on TRESGUERRAS, so the additional forenames are worth more than they were yesterday - but they are still tree-only. ***

column1: *** JUAN CARLOS LERENA - THE CENTRAL NULL, ON A THIRD PLATFORM ***
column2: *** EXACTLY ONE RESULT IN ALL OF GENEANET *** - "DEL CAMPO LERENA Juan Carlos", family tree of gdut, a compound in which Lerena is the SECOND surname
column4: *** He is absent from FamilySearch, absent from WikiTree, and absent from Geneanet. *** Three independent bodies of user genealogy, covering France, Spain, Uruguay and Argentina, and not one person has ever recorded him.

column1: CAROLINA LERENA VEGA
column2: b. 1824 Montevideo, d. 1892; m. JULIAN PELAYO MARTINEZ y DEL RIO (1845); died General Rodriguez, Buenos Aires. Trees of apiccione and fedegrifo
column4: *** NOT Carolina ORIBE, Luis's first wife *** - a different Carolina, of a LERENA VEGA branch, and one more Montevideo Lerena line this archive has never touched.
